svg.text: Three ceiling turrets each place one plain rod; all tools and vessels are passive loose parts;
nothing else hangs in the cell, and the rods hose the cell down themselves.
17 servo axes (3 hands × 5, press ram, turntable)
DRIVE ROOM (dry): ring drives, Z towers, ram, valves, filtered-air plenum
SERVICE (below deck): sump 10 L, pumps, boiler 6 L, chip box,
BT drive and load cells, 4 induction modules, extraction fan,
TOP VIEW of the deck (ceiling discs drawn transparent)
back wall · rear gutter · rails A, B · jet gates G1, G2
H3 · H2, H4 at the back
rod-axis reach Ø400 per turret (circles never touch)
How a hand works: two disc rotations in the ceiling place the rod (X-Y),
the rod slides (Z, 380 stroke) and turns (yaw); a core shaft inside drives tools.
Every tool, cup and vessel is a passive loose part that leaves for the washer.
A roll head on the rod adds a 190 mm offset, so neighbouring hands can
pass items: T1 → turntable → T2 → bench edge → T3 (about 5 moves per vessel).

g.text: 1/9 Box with potatoes is pushed through the port in the left wall onto the dock (load cells weigh every dose)
2/9 T1: discs turn, rod lowers; tongs on the roll head take a potato and drop it into the die cassette
3/9 Fixed press ram (3 kN) pushes it through the 10 mm grid; dice fall into a cup on the turntable
4/9 Turntable BT turns a quarter: the full cup moves from under the ram to T2's side
5/9 T2 takes the cup by its stub (roll head) and relays it to the bench edge, inside T3's tool reach
6/9 T3 takes the cup, rolls it over the pot on H1 (induction on) and pours; cup back to the bench
7/9 T3 takes the spoon-scraper from its rim rest and stirs; the pot simmers with its lid
8/9 Ready: lidded vessels and all used ware are relayed out through the port to the washer
9/9 Wash-down: each rod carries a jet lance on a fixed path; seam gaps flushed from the top (33 min, 33 L)
